planting.note: Plant bare-root trees in early spring in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Ya Li is a classic Chinese Asian pear cultivar with a distinctive bottle shape and thin, smooth, greenish-yellow skin, unlike the round, russeted Japanese-type Asian pears such as Hosui and Shinko.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic soil in full sun; requires a different Asian pear variety nearby for pollination, since it is not self-fruitful. Ya Li, meaning "duck pear" for its elongated, bottle-like shape, is one of the oldest and most widely grown Chinese Asian pear cultivars, producing medium to large fruit with thin, smooth, pale greenish-yellow skin quite unlike the golden-russeted surface of Japanese-type Asian pears. The white flesh is crisp, exceptionally juicy, and mildly sweet with a refreshing, delicate flavor, best enjoyed fresh at harvest since, like all Asian pears, it does not ripen further or improve in storage after picking. It is a vigorous, productive, and widely adaptable tree, valued in Chinese cuisine both fresh and cooked into sweet soups and simmered dessert preparations. Thin heavy fruit clusters to one fruit per spur for larger, better-quality pears, and watch for fire blight susceptibility common to the Asian pear group.
